name: The Game Awards
description: Geoff Keighley's annual video-game awards show, staged at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles with a live orchestra and streamed free across YouTube, Twitch and other platforms rather than sold to a television network. Keighley created it in 2014 after Spike dropped the Video Game Awards, and world premieres now carry as much of the running order as the trophies. The 2025 show drew 4.4 million peak concurrent viewers across western platforms.

name: Summer Game Fest
description: Geoff Keighley's June cross-platform showcase, the de facto successor to E3's summer slot. A roughly two-hour live main show anchors several days of Play Days hands-on sessions and partner streams. The 2026 edition moved from the YouTube Theater in Inglewood to the Dolby Theatre in Hollywood and was co-hosted by Lucy James.

sources.title: Live June 5, 2026 from Dolby Theatre in LA

name: Gamescom Opening Night Live
description: The two-hour showcase that opens gamescom, staged at Koelnmesse in Cologne on the evening before the fair's doors open and streamed worldwide. Geoff Keighley has hosted it since 2019; the 2026 edition added Eefje "sjokz" Depoortere as co-host. gamescom itself, run by Koelnmesse, is the largest games event in the world by attendance.

name: Evo
description: The Evolution Championship Series, the largest open-bracket fighting-game tournament in the world. Thousands of entrants play down on a hall floor for three days before the finals move to a main stage, broadcast on Twitch and YouTube. The Las Vegas flagship moved from its early-August weekend in 2025 to late June in 2026, and the brand now also runs Evo Japan and Evo France.

sources.title: Friday, June 26, 2026 through Sunday, June 28, 2026 at the Las Vegas Convention Center

name: The International
description: Valve's annual Dota 2 world championship, running since 2011 and the tournament that made crowdfunded esports prize pools famous. A Swiss-format group stage feeds an arena playoff; the 2026 edition was the fifteenth and put the main event in Shanghai's Oriental Sports Center, where Team Spirit became the first side to lift the Aegis three times.

name: League of Legends World Championship
description: Riot Games' annual League of Legends world championship, the largest esports broadcast of the year and the one with the most elaborate opening ceremony. The month-long 2026 run is split across three US venues: play-ins at the Riot Games Arena in Los Angeles, the Swiss stage and knockouts at the Credit Union of Texas Event Center in Allen, and the final at Barclays Center in Brooklyn.

sources.publisher: Credit Union of Texas Event Center
sources.title: Credit Union of Texas Event Center to Host Key Rounds of the 2026 League of Legends World Championship

name: Valorant Champions
description: The world championship that closes Riot Games' Valorant Champions Tour season. Sixteen teams play four GSL groups into an eight-team double-elimination playoff. Riot announced in August 2025 that the 2026 edition would be China's first, splitting the group stage and the playoffs between two Shanghai venues; it is also the last Champions of the franchised era before the VCT moves to open qualifiers in 2027.

sources.title: VALORANT: 2026 Champions Tour schedule, with dates and locations

name: Counter-Strike Major Championship
description: The Valve-sanctioned Counter-Strike world championship, run twice a year by a rotating cast of tournament organisers. Each Major opens with a 32-team qualifying stage in a studio before the last eight move to an arena for the playoffs. The 2026 cycle ran IEM Cologne in June, won by Team Falcons at the Lanxess Arena, and closes with PGL's Singapore Major, the first Major held in Southeast Asia.

sources.title: PGL unveils CS2 Singapore Major in 2026

name: Intel Extreme Masters
description: ESL's flagship Counter-Strike circuit, first run as the Intel Extreme Masters in 2007 and best known for the winter World Championship that filled the Spodek arena in Katowice. From 2027 that winter event moves to the Tauron Arena in Krakow, with 24 teams playing three stages into a four-day arena playoff.

name: Call of Duty League Championship
description: The season-ending playoff of the Call of Duty League, an eight-team best-of-seven bracket played over four days for a $2 million prize pool. The 2026 championship was hosted by FaZe Esports at the Michelob ULTRA Arena inside Mandalay Bay in Las Vegas, with ESL FACEIT Group as production partner; FaZe Vegas beat OpTic Texas 5-2 in the final.

name: Pokémon World Championships
description: The Pokémon Company's invitation-only world finals, run across four competitions at once - the Trading Card Game, video-game doubles, Pokémon GO and Pokémon UNITE - and streamed on the official Pokémon Twitch channel and the Play! Pokémon YouTube channel. The 2026 edition takes over San Francisco's Moscone Center alongside the first PokémonXP fan convention, with the Sunday finals staged at Chase Center.

name: Esports World Cup
description: A seven-week multi-title festival run by the Esports Foundation, with more than 20 game championships and a cross-game Club Championship on top. Held in Riyadh from its 2024 launch, the 2026 edition was relocated to Paris - the Paris Expo Porte de Versailles for most of the run, with Championship Sunday moved up to the Accor Arena after tickets sold out. AG.AL took the $7 million club title.

name: Rocket League World Championship
description: The season finale of the Rocket League Championship Series, run by Epic Games with BLAST. Twenty teams from seven regions play three closed days before the arena opens for a three-day public finals weekend and a $1.2 million prize pool. The 2026 edition returns to Dickies Arena in Fort Worth, the venue's third time hosting Worlds after 2022 and 2024.

name: Overwatch Champions Series
description: Blizzard's Overwatch 2 circuit, run with FACEIT since 2024 as the successor to the franchised Overwatch League. Regional leagues in North America/EMEA, Asia and China feed three international live events a year - Champions Clash in May, the Midseason Championship in the summer and the World Finals in December. The 2026 World Finals are China's first.

sources.title: OWCS Midseason Championship 2026: Results, teams, and more

name: League of Legends EMEA Championship
description: Riot's top-tier European League of Legends league, played almost entirely from the Riot Games Arena in Berlin - a purpose-built broadcast facility rather than a touring show. The 2026 season runs three tournaments (LEC Versus, Spring and Summer) with arena road trips to Paris, Madrid and a Summer Finals at the Palais Nikaia in Nice.

sources.title: Running from July 24 to September 20, the Summer Split is going to be huge

name: League of Legends Champions Korea
description: Korea's top League of Legends league, contested by ten teams and played out of CHZZK LoL Park in Jongno, Seoul. The 2026 season runs from mid-January to mid-September across the LCK Cup, two round-robin blocks and playoffs, with the finals weekend at the 15,000-seat KSPO Dome, the 1988 Olympic gymnastics arena.

sources.title: LCK Finals at KSPO Dome on September 12-13, Road to MSI in Wonju on June 12-14

name: PAX West
description: The original Penny Arcade Expo, created in 2004 by the authors of the Penny Arcade webcomic, held in Seattle since 2007 and now co-organised with RELX. Four days at the Seattle Convention Center over Labor Day weekend: an expo hall, panel theatres, tabletop halls, tournaments and a main-stage concert programme. Sibling shows run as PAX East in Boston, PAX Aus in Melbourne and PAX Unplugged in Philadelphia.

sources.title: PAX - a celebration of gaming and gaming culture

name: QuakeCon
description: id Software's annual gathering, running since 1996 and built around a 24-hour Bring-Your-Own-Computer hall where attendees haul in their own towers for four days of LAN play. Bethesda hosts it at the Gaylord Texan in Grapevine, with tournaments, tabletop, panels and a streamed programme; 2026 was the 30th anniversary.

venue.name: Gaylord Texan Resort and Convention Center

name: Gen Con
description: North America's largest and longest-running tabletop games convention, founded in 1968 and held since 2003 across the Indiana Convention Center, Lucas Oil Stadium and the connected downtown Indianapolis hotels. Thousands of ticketed events run in parallel - board games, card games, role-playing, seminars and a streamed programme.

name: Games Done Quick
description: A week-long speedrunning charity marathon broadcast around the clock from a hotel ballroom, with a live audience, couch commentary and donation incentives read on air. Two marathons run each year: Awesome Games Done Quick in January for the Prevent Cancer Foundation and Summer Games Done Quick in the summer for Doctors Without Borders. Streams on Twitch and, since AGDQ 2026, simulcast on YouTube. SGDQ 2026 in Minneapolis raised $2,409,821.

sources.title: Awesome Games Done Quick 2026 fires up with $2.4+ million raised for charity

name: Nintendo Direct
description: Nintendo's own video presentation format, premiered on YouTube and the Nintendo Today! app rather than staged for a live audience, and the way the company has announced its slate since 2011. A general Direct usually lands in February, June and September, with shorter game-specific and Partner Showcase editions in between; the June 2026 general Direct ran about 50 minutes and was followed by roughly 95 minutes of Nintendo Treehouse: Live gameplay.

name: PlayStation State of Play
description: Sony's PlayStation video programme, premiered on the official PlayStation YouTube and Twitch channels several times a year with no fixed calendar slot and trailed in advance on PlayStation.Blog. The June 2026 edition ran over 60 minutes and led with God of War Laufey and a Marvel's Wolverine gameplay look.

name: Xbox Games Showcase
description: Microsoft's annual June games presentation, the successor to its E3 briefing. Distributed across a wide platform list - YouTube, Twitch including a dedicated ASL channel, Facebook, Steam, Bilibili and, in the US, Amazon Live and Prime Video on Fire TV - and usually followed by a deep-dive Direct on one franchise. The 2026 show paired with a Gears of War: E-Day Direct.
